title: Three Sources, One Practice
intro: Checked against Erika Hall's *Just Enough Research* and Teresa Torres's *Continuous Discovery Habits*, this book has no conflicts.

learn.title: Three layers
learn.text:
**Hall — foundations.** Why research, how much, honest language, organisational research.
**Torres — discovery cadence.** The product trio, weekly touchpoints, opportunity solution trees, assumption tests.
**Calabro — execution.** Methods, rigor, biases, interaction evidence, proving impact.

Different questions, compatible answers.

try.q: Which source covers the weekly discovery cadence?
try.explain: Product trio, weekly touchpoints, opportunity solution trees.

learn.title: From Hall
learn.text:
**Five usability qualities** (Nielsen): learnability, efficiency, memorability, error recovery, satisfaction. Most studies only test the first.

**Never say “validate”.** It frames research as proving you're right. Say *evaluate* or *test*, and aim to be proven wrong.

**Cheap tests first:** paper before interactive, colleagues before recruited participants.

try.q: Why does Hall object to the word “validate”?
options: It frames research as proving you're right
It is too technical for stakeholders
It belongs to engineering, not research
try.explain: Say evaluate or test, and aim to be proven wrong.

learn.title: Where they sharpen each other
learn.text:
Hall's five usability qualities sharpen the usability-versus-concept-test argument: most studies only measure learnability.

Hall on “validate” pairs with the cognitive-biases article — the word invites confirmation bias before the study starts.

Torres's cadence answers a question Calabro mostly doesn't: how often to talk to users when nothing is broken.

try.q: Which question does Torres answer that Calabro mostly doesn't?
options: How often to talk to users when nothing is broken
How to run a usability test
